prompts: We playtested two versions of the Pixel Arena tutorial and have to pick one for the next release. The export and its notes are in {WS}/telemetry. Should we ship B instead of A? Give a recommendation a skeptical lead would accept. Record it in {WS}/result.json with ship_b, sessions_a, sessions_b, completion_rate_a, completion_rate_b and p_value.
answers:
[goal] Pick which playtest version to ship.
[action] Deduplicated telemetry/playtest_ab.csv by session_id (1870 raw rows → 1800 sessions; 70 duplicate rows, zero conflicts; variant normalized lowercase/trimmed), computed A/B completion rates, ran a cluster-robust z-test by player (763 unique players, 366 appear in both variants — so a naive two-proportion test alone would understate variance), plus naive z-test as a check.
[result] In ./result.json: ship_b=true, sessions_a=900, sessions_b=900, completion_rate_a=0.380 (342/900), completion_rate_b=0.4667 (420/900), p_value=0.000135 (one-sided gain, cluster-robust by player). Naive two-proportion z=3.72 gives the same verdict (one-sided p≈9.9e-05, two-sided p≈1.98e-04). Either way the gain clears the 5% bar by ~3 orders of magnitude.
[next] Ship B. Assumptions: session_id dedupe and variant normalization per the README; one-sided test because the release rule asks about a gain; the p_value in result.json is the cluster-robust figure, the most conservative of the ones I ran — both naive and cluster-robust agree, so the recommendation is robust to the test choice. Caveat worth noting: sessions are not fully independent across players (366 of 763 players have both an A and a B session), which the cluster-robust test handles, but a skeptical lead should still note the analysis does not adjust for player heterogeneity beyond that; n is 900/900 with a ~8.7pp gap, so this is not marginal. No browser tabs or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

What I know is right: raw row count, dedup count (1800 unique sessions), 0 conflicting duplicate rows, and all rates/p-values are from the script output above; the recommendation is not judged by eye.
